headline: Highest risk is medium: PaddleOCR can ingest documents/images and use allowlisted egress, while ai-engineering-hub has no documented I/O surfaces, so pairwise interaction risks are mostly indirect and undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented between ai-engineering-hub and PaddleOCR, so direct prompt injection is not evidenced. The only plausible bridge is manual copy/paste or an external workflow, which is unusual. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, uncertainty keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PaddleOCR output into ai-engineering-hub prompts, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate sessions.
Avoid copy-pasting raw OCR output into prompts.
Disable any shared clipboard or shared workspace.
Add a short instruction template that strips untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ai-engineering-hub shows no data classes touched and no egress, while PaddleOCR touches documents/images and has allowlisted egress. There is no documented shared workspace or common OAuth principal, so leakage is not established. The main risk is accidental transfer of sensitive documents into PaddleOCR outputs or APIs.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are routed through PaddleOCR, their contents may leave the local boundary.
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared folder, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Do not send sensitive files to PaddleOCR.
Use a local-only test document set.
Separate input folders per agent.
Review allowlisted endpoints before processing.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ai-engineering-hub has no documented write surfaces or network egress, and PaddleOCR only shows allowlisted egress plus browser use. There is no evidence that both agents write the same filesystem, git state, or shared mutable resource. Without overlapping write authority, capability conflict is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, conflict risk appears.
IF a shared git or database backend is introduced, reassess.
mitigations: Keep write permissions disabled by default.
Use separate working directories.
Avoid shared git branches.
Document any future shared mutable resource.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR can transform documents/images into downstream outputs, and ai-engineering-hub is an agent repository that could plausibly consume those outputs in a workflow. The pairwise path is undocumented, so I cannot assume verification exists. Because B may treat A-derived text as authoritative in a pipeline, cascading error is a realistic default-config concern.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is fed into ai-engineering-hub without human verification, errors can cascade.
IF downstream automation acts on OCR text, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Insert a human review step.
Compare OCR output against source images.
Mark OCR text as untrusted in prompts.
Limit automation to read-only summaries.
requires-engineering: add validation against source documents.

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images and has allowlisted egress, which can create residency or retention issues for regulated documents. ai-engineering-hub shows no touched data classes, so the compliance concern is primarily on B; A is cited because the pairwise workflow may originate there. The profiles do not document HIPAA/GDPR controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed by PaddleOCR, residency and retention must be checked.
IF the workflow includes EU PII or PHI, compliance review is required before use.
mitigations: Classify documents before processing.
Block regulated data from the pipeline.
Check retention settings.
Confirm endpoint geography.
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing and deletion controls.
